page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.sn1ne.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench categorize the processing capabilities as weak to poor, falling within the bottom 10% to 25% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read operations scoring in the bottom 10% at 19.1 GB/sec, and write operations in the bottom 25% at 17.26 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET operations are positioned in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is limited to 2.43 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower resource density, making it an entry-level option for workloads requiring dedicated compute resources without high memory or storage demands. However, the lack of bundled local storage and the poor memory bandwidth are notable tradeoffs. The instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale Redis deployments, or low-intensity background processing tasks that do not require high-throughput memory or storage performance.

It is best suited for low-intensity workloads, such as basic web serving, lightweight background processing, and small database operations that do not demand high memory bandwidth or local storage.
